item.title: Has U.S. inflation started turning higher again?
item.description: The average tariff rate on U.S. imports jumped from 2.6% to 13% over the course of 2025, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. On paper, that kind of increase should have pushed inflation higher. Instead, headline inflation actually eased from 2.9% year over year in December 2024 to 2.7% in December 2025. item.title: Germany Q4 final GDP 0.3% vs 0.3% q/q prelim
item.description: Prior 0.0%GDP Y/Y 0.4% vs 0.4% preliminaryPrior 0.3%No changes to the preliminary estimates. The German economy has been recovering gradually due to the expansionary fiscal policies and the ECB rate cuts. The momentum should hold in the first quarter given the strong data we had so far, unless there is a major slump in March. Economists expect the economy to grow about 1.0% in 2026, up from just 0.3% in 2025. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Ex-BoJ Governor Kuroda urges tighter policy; warns Takaichi stimulus could fuel inflation
item.description: In an exclusive interview with Reuters, former Bank of Japan chief, Haruhiko Kuroda expressed concerns about potential inflationary upswing coming from Takaichi's big spending plans and a weak yen. Kuroda is famous for leading the BoJ during the Abenomics era. He launched a massive monetary stimulus in 2013 in an attempt to bring Japan out of deflation. Now, Kuroda is calling for tighter monetary and fiscal policy as the economic context is the opposite of what he experienced in the last decade.
